rule.title: What the detector looks for
rule.transhipment: Pairs of vessels from AIS source {{sources}} or inside a {{zoneKinds}} that come within {{radius}} m of each other within {{window}} minutes are scored by speed × location × heading priorities. Pairs with accumulated priority are re-analysed with route interpolation and 30-minute sliding windows; a transhipment is reported when the score reaches {{threshold}} % (critical from {{critical}} %).
rule.fishing: A loitering pattern typical of fishing: at least {{minDuration}} minutes and {{minPositions}} positions at {{minSog}}–{{maxSog}} kn with a mean course change of at least {{rate}} °/min, inside a {{kinds}}.
rule.dark: A vessel stops transmitting AIS for more than {{gap}} minutes while it last sailed above {{sog}} kn more than {{distance}} km away from any global {{kinds}} zone. The event ends when the vessel reappears; gaps longer than {{maxGap}} hours are not reported.
rule.anomaly: The reported navigational status contradicts the status predicted from the vessel's motion for {{minPositions}} consecutive positions. The event ends at the first consistent position.
rule.geofence: A vessel enters an active {{kinds}} zone that raises an alert on entry (zone buffer included).
